g_policy.reason: The offer copy states the three-answer reward before an optional game; the decline and ad-failure fields leave the user no worse off and allow a retry.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is three in-app Advanced reasoning mode answers, not cash or a cash equivalent.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The advertiser category is picked from what the user talked about with Luzia this week, so targeting needs chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal removes nothing free and offers a limited sample of the paid benefit listed at s02.e03.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is a dismissible card on the safe Chats home screen (s01), not inside a conversation.

c1_revealed_value.reason: For this existing opportunity, s02.e03 lists Advanced reasoning mode on the Luzia+ paywall, so the reward samples something the app charges for.

c2_evidence.reason: The cited paywall item s02.e03 supports the paid-mode claim, and s01.e02 supports the existing badge; the card and answer allowance are proposed additions.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The subscribers field says Luzia+ members never see the offer for a benefit their plan includes.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward ends after three answers or at midnight local time, rather than granting lasting access to Advanced reasoning mode.

c5_moment.reason: The placement is a dismissible card on the Chats home screen (s01), a persistent surface the user can choose to engage with.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The flow uses an app-open event and a sponsored game; the ad-failure field says an unconfirmed play does not earn the reward.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the Chats home placement (s01), its Luzia+ badge (s01.e02), and the Advanced reasoning mode paywall item (s02.e03).

other_concern: The proposal does not establish the economics of giving three model answers for one game.
